construct: a glyph shared by (plain,sm) and (marked,lg) whose per-axis rectangle also COVERS (plain,lg) and (marked,sm), where the library draws no glyph at all
why: THE ANTI-OVERDRAW GUARD. A rectangularity test asserted only over the combos where the glyph is PRESENT cannot see the cells the library leaves EMPTY: the value sets tone{plain,marked} x size{sm,lg} look rectangular over the two drawn cells and would mint the glyph in four. Over-draw is the one class the fixture's captured-channel -> contract direction cannot measure, so it is measured here as a NAME: the asset must stay refused under svg-content-multi-axis. An ugly mint is worse than an honest refusal.

canvas.note: the conjunction rectangle covers cells the library leaves empty; the whole asset refuses and the host promotes as a box
